name: Vonage

field_reviews.reason: Live developer.vonage.com authentication concepts page: an API key and secret are created with every account and are the baseline credential; older APIs take them as request params, newer ones Base64-encoded via Basic auth.

Auth docs confirm all three: API key+secret, Basic Authentication (Base64 key:secret header on newer APIs), and RS256 JWTs generated from an application's private key; JWT recommended for Messages/Verify since Basic auth there does not support webhooks or ACLs.
Vonage getting-started docs confirm self-serve signup issues an API key and secret immediately with free trial credit; production usage is pay-as-you-go once a payment method is added.
CPaaS surface spans SMS, Messages (WhatsApp/RCS), Voice, Verify, Video, Numbers, Applications, and Reports APIs on the developer portal.

REST is the primary protocol, confirmed. However the draft lists official vendor MCP servers in mcp_status while omitting mcp from api_protocols, which is inconsistent with this batch's convention (Salesforce/Slack/Podio drafts include mcp in protocols when an official server exists). Value is defensible but incomplete; evidence for the MCP surface is the vendor's own MCP docs.

Vendor docs page (developer.vonage.com/en/mcp-server/...) confirms two official MCP servers: a Documentation MCP Server and the Server API Bindings (Tooling) MCP Server for managing apps, numbers, reports and sending messages. The npm package @vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings (latest 1.5.1) is maintained exclusively by vonage.com accounts — genuinely vendor-owned, not community.
Immediate self-serve credentials with trial credit; full public docs and SDKs.
No gate; trial restrictions (verified test numbers until payment method added) are standard CPaaS anti-abuse limits, not an access blocker.

notes: Re-verified auth concepts page (API key/secret, Basic, RS256 JWT), the vendor MCP introduction page (Documentation + Server API Bindings servers), and confirmed npm package ownership via the registry (all maintainers @vonage.com). Only quibble: api_protocols omits mcp despite official vendor MCP servers, inconsistent with sibling drafts — flagged PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rather than contradicted since rest genuinely is the primary API protocol and the MCP servers are developer tooling (docs search + account management) rather than a full API surface.
